resources.string: A simplified view of normal adult pelvic anatomy. The moving traces show the direction of flow in each duct, not the timing of secretion.
The paired seminal vesicles sit behind the bladder and above the prostate. The ejaculatory ducts pass through the prostate. The bulbourethral glands sit below it and drain farther downstream.
Each seminal vesicle contributes fructose-rich fluid through a short duct. This duct joins the widened end of the vas deferens on the same side to form an ejaculatory duct.
Each ejaculatory duct carries sperm from the vas deferens and fluid from the seminal vesicle. It passes through the prostate and opens into the prostatic urethra.
Multiple small prostatic ducts carry prostate secretions directly into the prostatic urethra. They open separately from the ejaculatory ducts; only a few are shown.
The paired glands lie below the prostate beside the membranous urethra. Their long ducts carry lubricating mucus past this segment and open farther downstream in the proximal spongy (bulbar) urethra.
OpenStax: accessory gland anatomy and physiology
Oblique pelvic cutaway, with one bulbourethral duct in focus
The prostate surrounds the prostatic urethra, above the level of the bulbourethral glands.
This short segment lies between the prostatic and spongy urethra. The bulbourethral glands sit behind and to either side of it; their ducts do not open here.
One gland is highlighted and its partner is shown behind it. Both are below the prostate in the deep perineal pouch and produce lubricating mucus.
The long duct passes through the perineal membrane and turns forward alongside the urethra before reaching its opening.
The duct opens on the floor of the bulbar urethra, the first part of the spongy urethra, downstream of the membranous segment.
